stories.title: New Zealand to introduce bill for under-16s social media ban
stories.summary: New Zealand is to introduce a bill seeking to ban under-16s from using social media. Under the latest proposals, platforms including TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat and Facebook, will have to take steps to check users are over 16 and platforms that fail to meet their obligations could face fines of up to 10% of their global revenue. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said social media was exposing children to "harmful content, addictive technology and pressures they are not equipped to deal with". But several political parties have said they will vote against the bill. The move follows a similar ban in Australia, while countries including the UK and Greece are set to introduce restrictions next year. Luxon said social media was affecting children's family life, mental health, sleep and education. "We have protections to keep children safe in the real world and we need them in the virtual world too," he said. New Zealand's government has not outlined which other "high risk" platforms could be impacted. A statement said that under the Online Safety Bill, which is being introduced to parliament on Monday, social media companies would be required to "take reasonable steps" to check users are over the age of 16 by using methods including existing account information, facial age estimation and digital identity checks. Platforms regularly used by children would also be required to regularly assess the risks they pose and report on how they are being identified and reduced. No penalties are proposed for children, parents or caregivers for breaches of the ban, but fines for social media companies could be substantially higher than in Australia, where the maximum penalty is $99m (£51.7m). It is unclear if the bill will get enough votes to pass however, after both the Act and New Zealand First (NZF) parties - which are coalition partners in the government - said they would oppose it.

stories.title: Russian troops liberate three communities in Ukraine operation over past day — top brass
stories.summary: The Ukrainian army lost roughly 1,400 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 24.

Russian troops liberated three communities in the Sumy and Zaporozhye Regions and the Donetsk People’s Republic over the past 24 hours in the special military operation in Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units took control of the settlement of Pershe Travnya in the Sumy Region through decisive operations.
<…> Battlegroup Center units liberated the settlement of Kucherov Yar in the Donetsk People’s Republic through active operations.
<…> Battlegroup East units advanced deep into the enemy’s defenses and liberated the settlement of Dolinka in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said in a statement.

The Ukrainian army lost roughly 1,400 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours, according to the latest data on the special military operation in Ukraine released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.

The latest figures show that the Ukrainian army lost roughly 235 troops and 11 motor vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup North, over 220 troops and three artillery guns in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup West and more than 255 troops, a German-made Leopard tank and two armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup South.

During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army also lost roughly 330 troops and six armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, over 315 troops and three armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup East and about 45 troops and two jamming stations in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup Dnepr, the latest figures show.
Russia’s Battlegroup North inflicted roughly 235 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed 11 enemy motor vehicles in its areas of responsibility over the past day, the ministry reported.

During the last 24-hour period, Battlegroup North units "inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of a mechanized brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Kiyanitsa and Pisarevka in the Sumy Region," the ministry said.

In the Kharkov direction, Battlegroup North units inflicted losses on formations of two mechanized brigades of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Veliky Burluk and Prikolotnoye in the Kharkov Region, the ministry reported.
The Ukrainian army lost an estimated 235 personnel and 11 motor vehicles in those frontline areas over the past 24 hours, it specified.

stories.title: Visit by head of The Vatican's diplomatic service marks return of diplomacy — expert
stories.summary: In recent years, diplomatic relations have been more informal, often conducted through special representatives such as Cardinal Matteo Zuppi for Ukraine
article_sentences: VATICAN, August 24.

Archbishop Paul Richard Gallagher, the Vatican Secretary for Relations with States and International Organizations, is to make a significant visit to Moscow, signaling a renewed phase of official diplomatic engagement.

Don Stefano Caprio, an associate professor at the Pontifical Oriental Institute and a renowned expert on the Russian world, shared his insights with TASS, emphasizing the importance of this development.
"This trip is highly significant; it marks the first official visit since 2021," Don Caprio explained.
"In recent years, diplomatic relations have been more informal, often conducted through special representatives such as Cardinal Matteo Zuppi for Ukraine.

Now, we are seeing a return to full-fledged official diplomacy." He further elaborated that the agenda extends beyond humanitarian mediation to encompass critical issues in the Middle East, Africa, and Ukraine.
"There is a clear commitment to seeking solutions across these regions, and previous efforts have laid the groundwork for meaningful dialogue," he added.
Don Caprio also recalled the initiatives proposed by Pope Francis and Pope Leo XIII for the Catholic Church to serve as a mediator or platform for negotiations.
While Russia has rejected such a platform, he noted that this does not equate to a rejection of dialogue altogether.
"The Holy See continues to play a moral role, fostering an environment conducive to diplomacy," he remarked.
In Don Caprio’s view, Gallagher’s visit exemplifies the Vatican’s reaffirmation of its diplomatic stance, including the Pope’s intention to restore functions to the Secretariat of State.
This is noteworthy given that Pope Francis has largely assumed these responsibilities, whereas Leo XIII previously managed them directly.
